headline: DAC developer to close its Middle East pilot and concentrate scale-up in Norway
summary: A direct air capture developer is shutting its Middle East pilot facility and refocusing its scale-up on Norway, per Quantum Commodity Intelligence — a siting decision consistent with pairing DAC with low-carbon power and North Sea storage.
co2crc_note: DAC siting logic (cheap low-carbon power + nearby storage) informs where atmospheric-removal capacity clusters; limited direct Australian relevance.
extractor_note: Developer unnamed and source paywalled/unfetchable; summary limited to headline-supported facts. Middle East pilot closure has a cancellation aspect but the overall story is a strategic relocation.

headline: Relae and Microsoft publish sixth-edition High-Quality CDR criteria with first delivery-risk framework
summary: Relae (formerly Carbon Direct) and Microsoft released the sixth edition of their Criteria for High-Quality Carbon Dioxide Removal, adding for the first time a delivery-risk framework (TECOP lens) that assesses whether a project will generate credits at the quantity and timeline promised to buyers — distinct from credit quality.
co2crc_note: CDR quality and delivery-risk standards shape buyer due diligence and project bankability across durable removals — relevant to Australian CDR/CCS project financing.
extractor_note: Relae = rebranded Carbon Direct; treated as a standards/advisory body (closest vocab: registry).

headline: Capsol Technologies wins five new carbon capture engineering studies
summary: Norwegian capture-technology firm Capsol secured five engineering studies across cement and energy, including a second site for a returning CapsolGo demonstration customer, boosting near-term liquidity for its hot potassium carbonate (HPC) capture technology.
co2crc_note: Incremental commercial traction for a European capture-tech vendor; limited direct CO2CRC relevance.
extractor_note: Underlying announcement 22 Sep (out of the strict daily window); surfaced as radar. Contracts signed but no discrete money figure stated.

headline: Idemitsu Americas backs InPlanet with non-recourse debt facility for enhanced rock weathering
summary: Idemitsu Americas Holdings and InPlanet closed a non-recourse debt facility to scale InPlanet's enhanced rock weathering carbon removal in Brazil, structured against a contracted, insured delivery of more than 28,500 tonnes of CO2 removal (2026-2028), with delivery insurance from CFC and broking by Howden.
co2crc_note: A Japanese energy major deploying non-recourse debt into durable CDR signals maturing carbon-removal project finance — relevant to CO2CRC's removal-market and financing watch.
extractor_note: Non-recourse debt facility (project finance), not equity. Facility size not disclosed (amount null). 28,500 t is a cumulative 2026-2028 delivery volume, not a per-annum capacity, so capacity_mtpa left null. Announced 17 Sep (out of strict daily window); surfaced as radar.
